knowledge:
- key_parameters: vcf=A VCF object from VariantAnnotation containing patient age stored as age in its colData ;; data=A data frame containing IndVar (logical indicator for exposure), sample_id, age, and columns of counts for all 96 trinucleotide mutations ;; factor=The exposure factor of interest (e.g., "Smoking" or "age") ;; object=A trained SuperSig S4 object ;; iupac=Logical indicating whether to use IUPAC labels to group trinucleotide features in simplify_signature ;; newdata=A data frame of new mutation data to predict on
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use when you have single-base mutations (exomic data) from cancer samples along with patient age and exposure/phenotype labels, and you want to identify supervised mutational signatures or predict exposure from mutational profiles.
- pitfalls: Patient age must be stored as age in the colData of the VCF object before running process_vcf. make_matrix requires installing and loading a reference genome (e.g., BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19 or BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38). The input data frame for get_signature must contain the IndVar column as the first column (or relocated) along with sample_id, age, and all 96 trinucleotide mutation counts. The apparent AUC returned in the S4 object is not cross-validated.

workflows.name: train_supersig
workflows.intent: Preprocess mutation data, build a trinucleotide feature matrix, and train a supervised mutational signature (SuperSig).
input: chr22.vcf.gz (VCF file containing single nucleotide variants)
example_dt (Data frame of mutations with sample_id, age, chromosome, position, ref, alt)
workflows.stages: 1. Read VCF and add patient age to colData ;; 2. Process VCF to a simplified data frame using process_vcf ;; 3. Transform mutations into a trinucleotide matrix using make_matrix ;; 4. Add the indicator variable (IndVar) to the matrix ;; 5. Train the supervised signature using get_signature ;; 6. Simplify the signature for visualization using simplify_signature
workflows.code:
vcf <- VariantAnnotation::readVcf(fl, "hg19") 
vcf <- vcf[, 1]
positions <- geno(vcf)$GT != "0|0" 
vcf <- vcf[positions[, 1],]
colData(vcf)$age <- 50
dt <- process_vcf(vcf)
input_dt <- make_matrix(example_dt)
input_dt <- input_dt %>%
  mutate(IndVar = c(1, 1, 1, 0, 0)) %>%
  relocate(IndVar)
set.seed(1)
supersig <- get_signature(data = input_dt, factor = "Smoking")
features <- simplify_signature(object = supersig, iupac = FALSE)
features_iupac <- simplify_signature(object = supersig, iupac = TRUE)

workflows.name: predict_supersig
workflows.intent: Apply a trained or pre-trained SuperSig to a new dataset to predict classification scores.
input: supersig_ls (Pre-trained SuperSigs list provided by the package)
workflows.stages: 1. Predict signature features and classification scores on new data using predict_signature
workflows.code:
newdata = predict_signature(supersig, newdata = input_dt, factor = "Smoking")
newdata = predict_signature(supersig_ls[["SMOKING (LUAD)"]], newdata = input_dt, factor = "Smoking")

workflows.name: partial_signature_adjustment
workflows.intent: Remove the contribution of a supervised signature from a mutation data frame to adjust for a confounding factor.
workflows.stages: 1. Adjust the mutation matrix by removing the signature's contribution using partial_signature
